title: Spring-mass oscillation

reference.basis: animated black-and-white scale bar with no stated real length

slow_motion.evidence: no caption, narration or visual indicator of slow motion; continuous animated oscillation

subjects.description: small orange rectangular mass hanging from the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: An orange block hanging from a vertical spring oscillates up and down in the plane of the image. The motion starts from a stretched-down position and continues as vertical oscillation through the end of the clip.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s-trace is a near-sinusoid with ~0.7 s period whose envelope slowly shrinks in air, as expected for a vertical mass on a spring. Undamped SHM is the textbook baseline, viscous damping gives exponential decay, and added quadratic air drag gives amplitude-dependent loss at large speed.

critique.finding: It says the block falls like a tossed rock with gravity {g}. It only partly captures the motion and misses the springy up-and-down.
critique.headline: Falling rock law chosen for bouncing spring block
critique.revision_idea: Add a spring pull back toward equilibrium with light damping. The misses swing from high to low with each bounce, exactly what a missing oscillation leaves behind.
critique.why_it_won: On the fitted frames it captures none of the repeated bouncing that the spring laws follow, leaving only the average fall.

headline: Falling rock law chosen for bouncing spring block
finding: It says the block falls like a tossed rock with gravity 4 ± 43 m/s². It only partly captures the motion and misses the springy up-and-down.

eyeball.law_in_words: At equilibrium mg equals k times static stretch, and small vertical oscillations have period T equals 2 pi sqrt(m/k), so g equals 4 pi squared times static stretch divided by T squared.

wonder.idea: Add a spring pull back toward equilibrium with light damping. The misses swing from high to low with each bounce, exactly what a missing oscillation leaves behind.
